title: Jonah and the Signal
premise: Jonah Eastwick smuggles forbidden memories through orbital customs, carrying the recorded last years of Meridian Colony—a settlement Earth officially erased. When a ghost name from her own buried past surfaces on the manifest of the Meridian, a ship that never launched, she realizes someone is hunting the colony's final signal and her along with it. Racing a decaying relay at the edge of dead space, Jonah must choose between broadcasting the truth that will destroy her family's legacy or letting the colony's dead stay forgotten. In the end she transmits the memories, sacrificing her anonymity and her brother's reputation, but winning the colonists their place in history—and finding, at last, where she belongs.
about_author: Mara Delacroix is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who spent six years at a remote listening station in the Atacama before turning to fiction. Her work explores what gets transmitted, what gets lost, and who decides which voices survive the static.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. A routine smuggling run through orbital customs introduces Jonah's trade in illegal memory-chips and her careful, practiced invisibility. She carries a shard of Meridian Colony footage she can't bring herself to sell. Emotional beat: the comfort and loneliness of a life built on not being seen.

chapters.title: The Name on the Manifest
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Fencing stolen shipping records, Jonah finds 'R. Eastwick' listed on the Meridian—a colony ship that never flew, crewed by a brother who supposedly died decades ago. Emotional beat: the floor drops out of her carefully constructed identity as the past reaches for her.

chapters.title: Static and Ash
chapters.summary: POV Jonah, flashback chapters in her brother Rowan's recorded memories. She plays the shard she's been hoarding and learns Meridian didn't fail—it was decommissioned, its people abandoned mid-signal, with Rowan among them. Emotional beat: grief curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: The Collector
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. A courteous stranger named Vess buys her entire inventory and offers a fortune for the Meridian shard—then reveals Earth's Bureau of Inheritance wants all colony records erased to protect a founding myth. Emotional beat: the hunter becomes visible, and so does the price of truth.

chapters.title: Dead Space Navigation
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Jonah steals a derelict hauler and recruits her only friend, customs officer Ilsa, who risks everything to forge her a flight corridor. Emotional beat: loyalty tested—belonging to a person versus belonging to a mission.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Arriving at the ancient relay, Jonah finds it dying and inhabited by Sef, a feral archivist raised on colony transmissions who has been faithfully re-broadcasting Meridian's loop into the void for years. Emotional beat: an unexpected mirror—someone else who refused to let the dead go silent.

chapters.title: What the Loop Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Sef. Inside the relay's archive, Sef shows Jonah the full transmission: Rowan's final log reveals the Bureau's decommission order was signed by the Eastwick family patriarch—her grandfather. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as complicity; the truth cuts both ways.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Vess's ship corners the relay; Ilsa arrives in a stolen cutter to buy Jonah time and is gravely injured in the exchange. Vess offers to let Jonah walk away if she surrenders the archive. Emotional beat: the climax of loyalty—Jonah refuses, choosing the dead over her own safety.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. With the relay failing, Jonah and Sef splice the colony's memories with Rowan's final log and her grandfather's signature into one unbroken signal, boosting it through the last window before Earth's transmission loop ends. Emotional beat: catharsis—truth released cannot be recalled.

chapters.title: The Long Echo
chapters.summary: POV Jonah, epilogue. Months later, Meridian's story is public; the Bureau fractures, and colonists' descendants claim their inheritance. Jonah, now visible and wanted, tends the rebuilt relay with Sef and recovering Ilsa. Emotional beat: resolution—belonging found not in invisibility, but in witness.
